success_patterns: The winning option mirrors the stem's own quantifier structure and parameter ranges literally. Examples: 'any 2-coloring' with ∀coloring ∃x,y; a constant depending on d,k and ε for all N≥2 and all β; the stem's own k, not k+1. Each distractor is a one-edit corruption: swapped quantifier order (∃y before ∀coloring), 'N sufficiently large' instead of N≥2, an ε-free constant, a shifted index, or a generalized class ('every finite coloring').

The winner is the plain positive theorem that uses every stem hypothesis and keeps the natural qualifiers, such as 'locally' homogeneous, the space H^{s+1}_loc matched to the local regularity of the data, open vs closed time interval, and 'exactly one' (existence AND uniqueness). Rejected options truncated it (existence only, or 'for every solution'), inflated it (closed [0,T], global H^{s+1}, 'globally homogeneous'), dropped a hypothesis (submersion type), or added a negative hedge ('Einstein need not persist').

For sharp estimates with explicit constants, the winner was the option whose constant follows from a mechanism (a heat-kernel or Hopf-Cole dimension count gives n/2, not (n-1)/2). The vague 'Cε(1+log(1+t/ε))' form is implied by the explicit one, and the t-uniform ε|log ε| bound fails for large t.

For long explicit case-split formulas, the winner passed internal-consistency checks and odd-one-out counting. Case ranges had to contain the endpoint that the option's own side clause refers to ('± = -1 iff w = N' needs w = N in the first case). An isolated shifted exponent or range, found by counting which placement most options share, was the corruption. A prose summary with no explicit formula lost to the fully explicit option when the stem asked for a complete classification.

For two-property or 'exact validity as the parameter varies' stems, the winner kept the properties separate (one unconditional, the other iff a clean condition such as countable). Distractors merged them (both iff, or both universal) or replaced the condition with a vaguer lattice-theoretic restatement.

patch.reasoning: A previous attempt to add a global 'star-center' rule hurt accuracy, so these edits are narrow and procedural. They record the concrete checks that separated winners from distractors in successful runs: literal mirroring of the stem's quantifiers and ranges, derivation of explicit constants by a mechanism, and internal-consistency tests on long explicit formulas. None of them tells the agent to default to the most elaborate or the most bare option.

edits.target: ## Tie-breaker: signature of the winning option
edits.content: - Mirror test: write the stem's quantifier order, parameter range and dependence list (e.g. 'any coloring', 'all N≥2 and all β', 'constant depending on d,k,ε') next to each option. The winner reproduces them literally. Reject an option that moves an ∃ before a ∀, restricts to 'large N', removes or adds a parameter dependence, shifts an index (k→k+1), or widens the class. Also check the time interval (open vs closed), the space (global vs _loc), and 'exactly one' vs bare existence or 'for every solution'. The spaces must match the regularity of the data given in the stem.

edits.target: ## Near-duplicate options: constants, quantifiers, ranges, exact details
edits.content: - Explicit constant vs vague 'C·(...)' form: an explicit coefficient is fine if you can obtain it from a mechanism (dimension count, Gaussian or heat-kernel normalization, scaling, a small case). If two options differ only in that coefficient (n/2 vs (n-1)/2), derive which one the mechanism gives. A vague 'Cε(1+log(1+t/ε))' bound is implied by the explicit-coefficient bound, so it loses on a 'strongest' stem. A bound without any growth in the large parameter (e.g. ε|log ε| uniform in t) must fail when the large-parameter regime is tested.

## Long explicit formulas and case-split options
- Check internal consistency before comparing with the source. (i) Each case range must contain the endpoint that the option's own side definitions refer to (a sign defined by 'iff w=N' requires w=N to lie in the case that uses it). (ii) The ranges together must cover the parameter domain without a gap or contradictory overlap (for example, a first case 'w≥0' that overlaps the 'otherwise' case). (iii) Count which placement of each exponent or bound is shared by most options. An isolated shift (ℓ^{N-w} vs ℓ^{N-w-1}) or a lone changed range is the single-edit corruption.
- An option that only describes the formula in words ('a three-case formula determined by ...') is a truncation. When the stem asks for a complete classification, it loses to the option that states every case explicitly and passes (i)-(iii).

## Multi-property stems ('exact general validity' of two properties)
- When a stem asks for the exact validity of two related properties over all parameters, test each property separately. A correct answer often separates them (one holds unconditionally, the other iff a simple condition). Distractors merge them (both iff, or both universal), swap which property is conditional, or replace the clean condition with a vaguer reformulation. Never accept 'because ...' glosses without checking that the reason actually implies the claim.
